hints: Complete the square to show $\Delta = 4(m-4)^2 + 4 > 0$ for all $m$.
walkthrough:
Equate the curve and line equations to form a quadratic equation in $x$:
$$2x^2 + m(2x + 1) = 6x + 4 \implies 2x^2 + (2m - 6)x + (m - 4) = 0$$

Calculate the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ of the quadratic equation:
$$\Delta = (2m - 6)^2 - 4(2)(m - 4) = (4m^2 - 24m + 36) - 8m + 32 = 4m^2 - 32m + 68$$

Complete the square for the quadratic expression in $m$:
$$\Delta = 4(m^2 - 8m) + 68 = 4\left((m - 4)^2 - 16\right) + 68 = 4(m - 4)^2 + 4$$
Conclude that since $(m - 4)^2 \ge 0$ for all $m \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Delta \ge 4 > 0$, so the line and curve always intersect at two distinct points.

ai_rubric.Discriminant and Intersections: Forms quadratic $2x^2 + (2m-6)x + (m-4) = 0$ (M1). Evaluates discriminant to $4m^2 - 32m + 68$ (DM1A1). Completes square to $4(m-4)^2 + 4$ (DM1). Concludes $\Delta > 0$ for all $m$ (A1).
